title: The Little Engine That Could
author: Watty Piper

hero.name: The Little Blue Engine
hero.description: Small blue steam locomotive with a friendly face, the determined hero of the story
hero.source_note: Named/distinctive character with face — source from Creative Fabrica or TPT clip art; generic Boardmaker train will not show the facial expression or blue colouring

ambiguous.issue: Could mean filled/carrying cargo (adjective) or slang meanings
ambiguous.reason: In this book it means the train cars are filled with toys and goods; search for 'full' or 'heavy load' if 'loaded' yields no result

ambiguous.issue: Could mean the top of the hill/mountain (location) or a spinning toy top
ambiguous.reason: Book climax is the engine reaching the top of the mountain; avoid toy top image

ambiguous.issue: Could show a person carrying bags or a vehicle carrying cargo
ambiguous.reason: The engine carries toys and food over the mountain; a vehicle/train carrying cargo is the correct image

notes: The mantra 'I think I can' is central to this book and maps beautifully onto the core words already on the board (I / think). Encourage educators to point to 'I' then 'think' on core during read-aloud. 'try' and 'help' are already in aac_extras so they do not need re-sourcing. The existing activity_images vocab (train, engine, hill, track, toys) overlaps well; 'hill' can substitute for 'mountain' if preferred. 'blue' is included as a fringe word because the Little Blue Engine is explicitly identified by colour throughout the story and students will use it to distinguish her from the other engines. Consider adding a secondary cell for 'heavy' engine / 'big' engine to contrast with the Little Engine if space allows on a companion board.
